name: SO Berlin Das Stue
positioning: Design hotel, now called Das Stue on its official site, in a 1930s former Royal Danish Embassy building in Berlin's embassy district, next to the Berlin Zoo and Tiergarten park
best_for: Design and art lovers who want Patricia Urquiola interiors in a historic embassy building
Travelers who want a quiet base beside the Berlin Zoo and Tiergarten park

facts.text: Das Stue sits in the heart of Berlin's embassy district.
The hotel is next to the Berlin Zoo and Tiergarten park.
The hotel occupies a 1930s neoclassical stone building that was once home to the Royal Danish Embassy.
The high-ceilinged lobby has an original white marble staircase.
Designer Patricia Urquiola furnished the lobby with modern furnishings of her own design and leather animals.
Photographs by Diane Arbus and Helmut Newton hang on the walls.
Rooms are spread through the landmark building and a newer annex.
Patricia Urquiola designed the room interiors, mixing modern and classic furnishings, rich fabrics and warm woods.
Bathrooms have rain showers and/or freestanding bathtubs.
The hotel has an indoor pool and a sauna.
The hotel can pick guests up from Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER).

highlights.text: The hotel is godparent to a kangaroo named Stuy at the Berlin Zoo.
Guests get exclusive access to the neighboring zoo via the bar's terrace, skipping the entrance lines but still paying for a ticket.
Some rooms have lofty ceilings and huge windows with views of the zoo and Tiergarten.
The public spaces display mesh sculptures of monkeys by Benedetta Mori and a crocodile head by Quentin Garel.

considerations.text: Rooms are split between the landmark building and a newer annex, so not every room is in the historic embassy building.
The zoo access via the terrace skips the entrance lines, but guests still pay for a zoo ticket.
WhataHotel notes it is a boutique hotel with limited room inventory.
